decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom carries heavy development investment and a public commitment to a growing proton therapy market, so management keeps it and blames any slow uptake on long hospital procurement cycles and pandemic delays.
Small volume chambers are core to the firm's precision dosimetry identity, cost little to maintain, and serve the growing small-field and SRS demand, so there is no reason to drop it.

Despite its overlap with Product B, the sunk certification and calibration costs and the need to justify the recent launch lead management to keep it and treat weak sales as temporary disruption from 2020 to 2021.
The multi-model standard clinical chamber line is central to the established calibration and dosimetry business that funds the cloud-platform direction, so it stays.
Thimble chambers are staple reference instruments backed by accredited calibration services with steady clinical demand, so the firm keeps it.
